full_text_checked: AlphaRefine: full arXiv v3 text extracted with PyMuPDF and read (Sec. 1-5, Tables 1-11, Fig. 1-8 captions). Code files opened: pytracking/refine_modules/refine_module.py (RefineModule.refine, branch_selector), pytracking/refine_modules/utils.py (mask2bbox fallback), ltr/actors/ar_actors/SEcm.py (losses), ltr/train_settings/SEx_beta/SEcm_r34.py (objective, jitter factors), arena/LaSOT/run_dimp_RF_mask.py (how the refined box is written back into DiMP state), arena/LaSOT/common_path.py (selector_path = 0); refine_module_vot20.py and run_RF_RF.py only grepped. RBO: full arXiv v1 text read (Sec. 1-5, Tables 1-5, Fig. 1-6 captions). Code opened: SiamRPN++-RBO/pysot/models/loss.py (Rank_CLS_Loss, Rank_IGR_Loss), pysot/models/model_builder.py (loss combination), pysot/core/config.py and experiments/train/fulldata/config.yaml (weights and thresholds). SiamBAN-RBO / SiamPW-RBO code and supplementary material not opened; no code was run. Related heads (RankDetNet, SiamRCR, SiamLTR) not opened.
inputs_state_output: AlphaRefine: inputs = RGB reference crop of the first frame (2x the ground-truth box, 256x256) and RGB test crop centred on the base tracker's current box (search factor 2.0, 256x256); ResNet-34 backbone shared, stride-16 features (reference 8x8, test 16x16); pixel-wise correlation (each of the 64 reference feature pixels is a 1x1 kernel, giving a 64-channel response map that keeps target-part layout); outputs = corner heatmaps (top-left, bottom-right) decoded with soft-argmax into a box, plus an auxiliary U-Net mask head used in training (off at inference by default). Internal state: only the fixed first-frame reference features (forward_ref once per video); no temporal memory, no update. RBO: standard Siamese tracker (template 127x127 from the first frame, search 255x255), dense per-location classification and regression maps; RBO changes only offline losses, no extra state or inference component. Ours: bounded grey crop around the ByteTrack prediction into FlyVis (721 hexal columns, 34 cell types), recurrent state running over 4 exemplar frames and then search frames, ridge target model on exemplar frames, readout = 68 region-pooled activity features per real detection region + observed-target descriptor + 8 geometry + 6 assignment-context features, output = score per candidate action (transfer full box of a real region, unmatched) against a fixed no-action logit 0. Key contrasts: (1) AlphaRefine keeps a spatial response map all the way to the head (corner heatmaps), while our readout pools activity per region into 68 numbers before any comparison with the target - exactly the RCNN-style pooling that AlphaRefine found worst; (2) AlphaRefine compares exemplar and search by part-wise correlation, our readout compares by a ridge model over pooled features; (3) both RBO and AlphaRefine produce boxes inside one object hypothesis, while our action chooses among several real detections, i.e. an identity decision.
action_and_refusal: AlphaRefine has no refusal: in the released code the refined box unconditionally overwrites the base tracker's state (arena/LaSOT/run_dimp_RF_mask.py: tracker.pos, tracker.target_sz and tracker.target_scale are replaced every frame after RF_module.refine). There is no score comparing refined vs base box and no keep-base option. The only fallbacks are internal: mask2bbox falls back to the corner box when the predicted mask is empty or smaller than 100 px area (pytracking/refine_modules/utils.py), and an optional branch_selector (int or learned network) chooses among AlphaRefine's own heads (bbox/corner/mask); the released LaSOT setting uses selector_path = 0 (always corner). The paper states AlphaRefine 'is not capable of tracking by itself' because of its 2x search region: it cannot move the track to another object, so its harm is bounded to box-size/position errors around the base answer. RBO: no abstention either; the tracker picks the highest-scoring location each frame. Only code-level analogue of refusal: for negative training pairs (template and search from different videos, DATASET.NEG = 0.2) there are no positives, and Rank_CLS_Loss pushes the softmax-weighted expectation of hard negatives (probability > 0.5) below 1 - margin = 0.5, i.e. it teaches that when the target is absent no candidate should exceed a fixed level. Ours: full-box transfer of a selected real region into the track state before native matching, with explicit unmatched option and fixed no-action logit 0. Our action can change identity (high harm), which is the reason a refusal is needed; AlphaRefine's always-on policy is justified only because its action cannot jump to another object.
labels_and_loss: AlphaRefine: synthetic labels from ground truth only. Training pairs = two frames of one video at most 50 frames apart; test crop centre/scale jittered around the ground truth (center and scale jitter factor 0.25, Eq. 2-4); label = ground-truth box in crop coordinates (x1,y1,x2,y2) and the object mask when available. Loss = MSE on corner coordinates + lambda * BCE on mask (lambda = 1000 when the corner loss is MSE; mask loss only for samples that have a mask, SEcm.py). No negatives, no absent target, no 'wrong object' samples, no class imbalance handling; data: LaSOT, GOT-10k, ImageNet VID/DET, COCO, YouTube-VOS, saliency sets; 40 epochs x 500 iterations x 256 pairs. RBO: labels from standard anchor/point assignment (positives by IoU with ground truth, negatives otherwise; 20% negative pairs from different videos). Loss = original CE + smooth-L1/IoU loss (weights 1.0 and 1.2) + 0.5 * classification ranking loss + 0.25 * IoU-guided ranking loss. Classification ranking (Eq. 6-8, Rank_CLS_Loss): per image, take positives' probabilities (mean, P+), take negatives sorted by probability, keep top n+ of them and only if some exceed 0.5, form a softmax-weighted expectation P-; loss = (1/beta) log(1 + exp(beta (P- - P+ + alpha))), alpha = 0.5, beta = 4; images without hard negatives are skipped; images without positives use P+ := 1 (hard negatives pushed below 0.5). This is a listwise, per-image (per-query) comparison that ignores easy negatives - a direct remedy for imbalance where a few distractors decide the outcome. IoU-guided ranking (Eq. 9-10, Rank_IGR_Loss): over all pairs of positives, exp(-gamma (p_i - p_j)) when IoU_i > IoU_j (pushes score order to follow IoU order), plus exp(-gamma (IoU_i - IoU_j.detach())) when p_i > p_j (only the higher one's regression is pushed), gamma = 3. Neutral events: no explicit neutral class; easy negatives are simply excluded from the ranking term. Rare positives: one positive suffices per image in the authors' argument ('as long as one positive sample ranks higher than the hard negative ones'). Ours: per-action MSE to good-minus-harm in {-1, 0, +1}, dominated by 0 (neutral), then softmax with fixed logit 0 and threshold; no pairwise or per-query comparison, so helpful actions are never trained to be above neutral ones of the same query.
data_camera_resolution_rate: AlphaRefine: training on LaSOT train (1120 videos), GOT-10k train (~10k videos), ImageNet VID/DET, COCO, YouTube-VOS, saliency datasets; evaluation on LaSOT test (280 videos, Tables 2-3, 5-8), TrackingNet test (511, Table 9), GOT-10k test (180, Table 10), VOT2020 (60, Table 11); ablations on LaSOT test with SiamRPNpp base (no separate validation split reported). Generic single-object tracking, handheld/moving cameras, native benchmark frame rates (not studied); input 256x256 RGB crops at 2x object size; initial condition = first-frame ground-truth box. Each result averaged over five runs (Sec. 4). RBO: PySOT training protocol (COCO, ImageNet VID/DET, YouTube-BB etc. [uncertain: exact list not re-checked in config]; GOT-10k train only for GOT-10k test); evaluation on OTB100 (100), UAV123 (123), TC128 (128), NFS30 (100), VOT2016 (60), GOT-10k test (180), LaSOT test (280); ablation on the pooled 352 sequences of TC128 + NFS30 + UAV123 (also test benchmarks). Template 127x127, search 255x255 RGB; initial condition first-frame box. Ours: BDD100K MOT, 1280x720 at 5 Hz annotation [uncertain: frame rate of our bench not re-checked here], moving ego camera, multi-object, grey bounded eye crop into 721 hexals, videos grouped train26 / fit20 / fit84 / val, initial condition from YOLO26s detections and ByteTrack.
metrics_and_numbers: AlphaRefine Table 1 (LaSOT, oracle: search region always centred on ground truth): AUC SiamRPNpp 0.682, ATOM 0.580, DiMPsuper 0.693, ECO 0.496, AlphaRefine 0.762.

AlphaRefine Table 2 (LaSOT test, AUC %, base -> base+AR): ECO 36.9 -> 46.1; RT-MDNet 30.8 -> 49.9; SiamRPNpp 47.6 -> 55.9; ATOM 49.5 -> 57.0; DiMP50 55.9 -> 60.2; DiMPsuper 63.7 -> 65.3. Gain shrinks as the base tracker's own box estimator gets better.
AlphaRefine Table 4: added latency about +5.1 to +5.7 ms per frame (2080Ti class GPU).
AlphaRefine Table 5 (head options, SiamRPNpp base, LaSOT AUC %): base 47.6; ARrpn 50.2; ARrcnn (global pooling + FC) 48.9; ARcorner 54.6; ARrpn+mask 53.7; ARrcnn+mask 51.6; ARcorner+mask 55.9.
AlphaRefine Table 6 (fusion, LaSOT AUC %): pixel-wise 55.9; depth-wise 54.8; naive 53.1.
AlphaRefine Table 7 (refiner comparison, LaSOT AUC %): SiamRPNpp 47.6; +IoU-Net 48.8; +SiamMask 50.3; +AR 55.9.
AlphaRefine Table 8 (backbone, LaSOT AUC %): ResNet-50 56.2, ResNet-34 55.9, ResNet-18 55.0.
AlphaRefine Tables 9-11: TrackingNet AUC e.g. DiMPsuper 77.6 -> 80.5; GOT-10k AO DiMPsuper 67.2 -> 70.1; VOT2020 EAO (baseline) DiMPsuper 0.314 -> 0.471.

RBO Table 4 (ablation, pooled TC128+NFS30+UAV123, 352 sequences, AUC %): SiamRPN++ 57.93 -> +CR 60.63 -> +CR+IGR-ori(RankDetNet form) 60.87 -> +CR+IGR 62.08; SiamBAN 59.61 -> +CR 61.15 -> +CR+IGR-ori 60.92 -> +CR+IGR 62.24.
RBO Table 2 (GOT-10k test): SiamRPN++ AO 51.7 -> 60.2; SiamPW-RBO AO 64.4.
RBO Table 3 (VOT2016 EAO): SiamRPN++ 0.463 -> 0.512; SiamBAN 0.502 -> SiamBAN-RBO 0.543.
RBO Fig. 5 (LaSOT success AUC): SiamRPN++ 0.496 -> SiamRPN++-RBO 0.532; SiamBAN 0.513 -> SiamBAN-RBO 0.524 (consistent with the text: gains of 3.6 and 1.1 points).

These are single-object tracking AUC/AO/EAO on generic benchmarks; they must not be translated into expected HOTA changes on our BDD100K MOT bench.
distinguishing_ablations: AlphaRefine: (1) Head ablation (Table 5) isolates 'keep spatial structure to the head': corner heatmaps with soft-argmax beat RPN-style per-location boxes by 4.4 AUC and RCNN-style global-pooled FC by 5.7 AUC (without mask); the authors explicitly argue RCNN style 'crashes spatial information' and RPN style has 'inconsistency because most precise box predictions may have a low score'. (2) Auxiliary mask supervision adds +1.3 to +3.5 AUC for every head (Table 5), i.e. dense pixel-level supervision during training improves the box even when the mask is not used at inference. (3) Fusion ablation (Table 6): pixel-wise > depth-wise > naive correlation (55.9 / 54.8 / 53.1). (4) Comparison with other refiners (Table 7) and backbones (Table 8). Mandatory components for the claimed effect: spatially preserved fusion + spatial (heatmap) head; the mask head is helpful but secondary. Runs: each result averaged over five runs, no CI or per-video spread; ablations use the LaSOT test set itself (no validation split) and one base tracker (SiamRPNpp). Missing: no ablation of when refinement hurts, no per-frame harm analysis, no gate between base and refined box, no evaluation of search-region centre error beyond the oracle of Table 1. RBO: (1) Table 4 separates classification ranking (CR, +2.70 / +1.54 AUC) from IoU-guided ranking (IGR, further +1.45 / +1.09); the original RankDetNet coupled form (IGR-ori) gives ~0 or negative change (60.63 -> 60.87; 61.15 -> 60.92), so the decoupled form with a detached lower IoU is the necessary detail. (2) Two-stage hard-negative mining with CE is reported as failing (target suppressed together with distractors), but only qualitatively (Fig. 6), no number. (3) Limitation stated by authors: gain on transformer tracker is much smaller (Table 5). No seeds, no CI, ablation on test benchmarks; one run per setting is implied [uncertain].

explanations_addressed.lost_discriminative_spatial_information_: Direct evidence (in a different task): AlphaRefine Tables 5-6 show that pooling the correlation map into a vector (RCNN head) or blurring with whole-template correlation loses the information needed for precise localization, and that part-wise (pixel-wise) correlation plus a spatial heatmap head recovers it. This is the closest published ablation to our 68 region-pooled features per detection region. Caution: their target is box precision on the right object, not choosing between objects.
explanations_addressed.target_vs_neighbour_identification: Design analogy: RBO's classification ranking loss is aimed exactly at distractors of the same class (hard negatives) and gains +1.5 to +2.7 AUC on pooled benchmarks (Table 4); Fig. 4 shows suppressed distractor responses. AlphaRefine does not address it (2x search region assumes the base tracker is on the right object).
explanations_addressed.training_objective_mismatched_to_final_a: Direct design evidence: RBO is an explicit argument and ablation that independent per-sample losses (CE + regression) misalign the score used for the final argmax selection with the quality of the selected output, and that a per-query ranking loss over candidates fixes it. Our per-action MSE regression followed by a softmax/threshold policy is the same mismatch: the policy uses the ordering of scores within a query and relative to the zero logit, but the loss never constrains that ordering. AlphaRefine also notes the RPN-head inconsistency (precise boxes with low score) as a reason to avoid score-based selection.
explanations_addressed.rare_useful_events_with_high_harm_cost: Partially / caution: RBO handles imbalance by ignoring easy negatives and comparing an expectation over the top hard negatives with the positives (margin 0.5), and in no-positive images pushes hard negatives below 0.5 - a mechanism for 'nothing should beat the threshold'. Neither paper models harm cost; AlphaRefine runs without refusal because its action has bounded harm, which is a caution that its always-on design does not transfer to our identity-changing action.
explanations_addressed.insufficient_history: Not addressed: both use only the first-frame template; AlphaRefine's reference branch is fixed after initialization.
explanations_addressed.limits_of_the_action_itself: Caution: AlphaRefine's oracle (Table 1) and its 2x search region show that refinement only helps when the coarse position is already right; our analogue is that full boxes in the eye give oracle +5.24 pp but 334 of 895 unfixable errors have the correct detection outside the eye. Neither paper extends the action range.

evidence_strength: Both peer-reviewed (CVPR 2021, CVPR 2022) with official public code (verified by opening loss/actor/inference files, not run). AlphaRefine is widely reused as a plug-in refiner in later trackers [uncertain: no independent replication checked here]; RBO has a small code base (36 GitHub stars) and no independent replication found in this short check. Overall: moderate for the general claims (spatially preserved fusion/heads improve box precision; per-query ranking losses align score with selection), weak for our decision because both are single-object, in-distribution, test-set ablations without CI, and neither evaluates refusal or harm.
difference_from_tried: AlphaRefine: the box-transfer part of our action is already 'refinement with a full box', and our boxes come from real detector regions, so box precision is not our bottleneck; what differs is its readout - pixel-wise exemplar-to-search correlation and a spatial (heatmap) head instead of region-pooled features and a ridge model. We have not tried a part-wise correlation readout over the FlyVis hexal lattice; the fixed/learned 3-peak association used peaks of the D map, not a part-wise correlation tensor. Its always-on policy is not new to us and is not suitable. RBO: differs from everything tried in the loss: we used per-action pointwise MSE (good-minus-harm) with a softmax-threshold policy; we never trained a within-query listwise/pairwise ranking where the helpful action must exceed both the neutral actions of the same query and the no-action logit by a margin, with easy neutrals excluded and no-positive queries pushed below the no-action logit. Overlap: the counterfactual/advantage objectives of item A02 address the same mismatch from the policy-learning side; RBO adds a concrete, tested ranking form and the decoupled IoU-ordering detail.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout loss (and optionally readout structure) of the FlyVis path; FlyVis core, eye and state unchanged in step 1. Change A (cheap, loss only, RBO analogue): per query (one track at one frame with its candidate actions and the no-action option fixed at logit 0) train the action scorer with (i) a classification ranking term: helpful actions (good-minus-harm = +1) must exceed max(0, softmax-weighted expectation of the top-k scored non-helpful actions) by margin alpha, logistic loss with beta as in RBO; actions scored below a hard threshold are ignored (easy neutrals); (ii) a no-positive term for queries without any helpful action: the softmax-weighted expectation of the top-k action scores must stay below 0 - alpha (the fixed no-action logit), which is the RBO negative-pair branch and directly targets 'abstain unless helpful'; (iii) harmful actions additionally ranked below neutral ones (pairwise, as in the IGR ordering term, with the lower item detached). Policy stays argmax with no-action at 0 and one threshold chosen on fit20; this keeps the action and the pre-registered comparison identical, so only the loss differs. Why it fixes a FlyVis problem: the readout of FlyVis activity is currently trained with an objective that does not constrain the ordering used by the decision, which our diagnostics show (13-33 outcome-changing actions among 1000-3500 selected; probabilities never above ~0.6; many seeds abstain completely). Change B (spatial readout, AlphaRefine analogue, only if A shows ordering signal but not enough): replace the 68 region-pooled features by a part-wise correlation map between the exemplar hexal activity (each exemplar hexal column, 34 cell types, as a 1x1 kernel) and the search-frame activity on the 721-hexal lattice, followed by a small heatmap head that scores each detection region by sampling the map inside its box; optional auxiliary dense target (target mask/box occupancy on hexals) as AlphaRefine's mask supervision. Equal controls for both: same loss and policy on (1) old D readout features (current version), (2) stock C, (3) eye input R1 (pooled grey pixels per region, no FlyVis), (4) no-fly geometry + assignment context only; FlyVis result only if D-with-ranking > no-fly-with-ranking, per project rule 6.16. Cheap distinguishing check on saved data (CPU): reuse the saved per-row features and outcome labels of z13_box_supervision_followup_v1 (fit20 4183 rows; fit84) and, with video-grouped cross-validation, compare MSE vs ranking heads on decision-relevant metrics before any HOTA: per-query top-1 hit rate on queries with a helpful action, within-query AUC helpful-vs-neutral, fraction of selected actions that change the outcome at matched coverage, and the oracle-normalized reserve captured on fit20 calibration. Proceed to the full replay/HOTA stage only if, on held-out videos, the ranking head with D features (a) captures a reserve whose paired-bootstrap lower bound exceeds 0 and (b) beats the no-fly geometry control with a positive lower bound on the within-query metric; otherwise stop Change A and record the node. Change B requires per-hexal activity maps, which do not appear to be in the saved run cache (per-video JSON files of ~37 KB) [uncertain], so it needs new FlyVis passes.
strongest_objection: Both sources improve ordering of candidates that are dense, plentiful (thousands of locations per image) and labelled by IoU with a single target on in-distribution benchmarks; our positives are about 5% of rows, a few dozen outcome-changing events in fit20, and labels are ternary consequences of a downstream assignment. A ranking loss cannot create discriminative information that the 68 pooled features lack; if the helpful-vs-neutral separation is absent in the features, the ranking head will either still abstain or learn context/geometry cues equally available to the no-fly control, giving no FlyVis result. AlphaRefine's gains are on box precision of the already-correct object, which is not our failure mode (identity choice and refusal), and its unconditional overwrite is the opposite of what our high-harm action needs.
cost_and_hardware: Change A: CPU only on saved features and labels; a few hours of implementation and minutes per seed for 24 heads (same scale as the latest CPU run), plus one replay/HOTA evaluation if the gate passes. Change B: needs new FlyVis activity maps per hexal over exemplar and search frames; FlyVis (734 parameters) fits easily on one 12 GB GPU, cost dominated by re-running crops for fit/val videos (hours of GPU [uncertain]); head training on CPU or GPU; requires author permission as a longer GPU run.
